title: Media Release: April 2026 Fuel Price Determination
text:
Media Release
April 2026 Fuel Price Determination
10 April 2026
The Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission wishes to assure the public that the April
2026 fuel price determination was made using the established pricing methodology and in
accordance with FCCC’s statutory role to regulate prices while ensuring the continued
availability of essential goods.
As a small import-dependent economy, Fiji is affected by international fuel prices and freight
costs that are determined beyond its shores and which our nation does not have the ability to
influence. With only three fuel suppliers operating domestically, the country's ability to negotiate
alternative supply terms is further limited, making careful regulation especially important in
periods of market instability.
Fuel prices in Fiji are reviewed each month using the least cost methodology, which takes into
account international refined fuel prices based on the Mean of Platts Singapore (MOPS),
together with international freight and exchange rates of the price setter. Typically, this process
operates with a one-month lag, meaning local prices generally reflect earlier import costs rather
than immediate market movements.
The April 2026 review was carried out during a period of exceptional volatility in international
fuel markets. During this time, FCCC observed that February 2026 stock was being depleted
more quickly than usual, while replacement supply was being secured in a significantly higher-
cost environment.
In light of these conditions, FCCC extended the pricing reference window beyond the usual one-
month period to include an additional 20 days of the subsequent month, so that the assessment
reflected a more representative picture of market movements and replacement costs during a
period of rapid change. The adjustment made in this instance reflected the need to respond
appropriately to market conditions that had moved beyond the usual parameters.
This approach remained consistent with the underlying methodology and was applied to support
the accuracy, stability and fairness of pricing outcomes. The April 2026 determination continued
to be based on the same core framework, including MOPS benchmarks, freight and exchange
rate considerations.

Since the conflict in the Gulf region began this year, FCCC has been closely monitoring
international fuel and LPG market movements, freight costs, foreign exchange pressures,
domestic stock positions, and broader supply chain developments. This has included daily
monitoring of stock levels on the ground and with suppliers.
A balanced approach was therefore taken in the April 2026 review. FCCC did not simply pass
through all international cost movements immediately but considered how best to moderate the
impact on families and businesses while also supporting continuity of supply.
It is also important to understand that these adjustments do not mean oil companies are making
additional profits. Fuel prices in Fiji are regulated, and margins are controlled. The changes
reflect the actual cost of bringing fuel into the country under prevailing market conditions.
FCCC remains committed to regulating fairly, transparently, and responsibly and will continue to
monitor the market closely and take the necessary steps to support both consumer protection
and supply stability. Any trader found overcharging, hoarding, and engaging anti-competitive
behaviour, in breach of the FCCC Act 2010, will be investigated and appropriate action taken.
-Ends-
